comparator.name: Bachelor Informatica (Computer Science)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 official study guide lists 12 compulsory 5-EC propedeutic courses (60 EC), 15 compulsory 5-EC postpropedeutic courses (75 EC), the compulsory 15-EC Afstudeerproject and 30 EC of genuine free elective space. This is 180 EC. OU uses a flexible part-time schedule, so its programme components are retained without forcing them into UCR semester dates.

alternatives.concept: Builds a computing programme around programming, networks and operating systems, databases, software development, algorithms and mathematical foundations, with data and AI applications. It captures significant OU Informatica content but cannot reproduce the full specialised programming, architecture, security, testing and compulsory capstone sequence.

alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, algorithms, data and research methods but organises the programme around how information systems serve users and organisations. alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The second route replaces specialist computer-science mathematics, software, systems and advanced AI courses with organisational research, product design, digital transformation, sociology, leadership and communication. These changes serve the officially recognised information-systems line and its social and organisational applications, and exceed the required four-course difference from the first route.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad software, systems, mathematics, data, security and research interests. The OU information-systems learning line supports a second, substantively distinct UCR curriculum centred on organisational and user-facing digital systems. The remaining communication-technology direction would require a sustained telecommunications or network-infrastructure sequence; the current UCR catalogue supplies one Networks & Operating Systems course and related communication study but no credible 24-course specialist programme. Production therefore stops at two.

notes.text: OU Informatica has compulsory architecture, object-oriented and functional programming, formal languages, distributed algorithms, operating systems, security, software testing, multiple integrated projects and a 15-EC final project. UCR offers meaningful computing and information-systems routes, but neither reproduces that full specialist sequence. OU also retains 30 EC of genuinely open elective space.
